item.title: The long one
item.description: Soil is the slow part of a garden and the part that pays back the longest. Every season the beds lose a little of what made them dark and loose, and every season something has to go back in. Leaves, grass, kitchen scraps, straw and old potting mix all have a place in the heap. The heap wants air and water in about the measure a wrung sponge holds, and it wants turning when it cools. A fork and ten minutes a week are enough for a small plot. In spring the finished compost goes on the beds an inch deep, and the worms carry it down. In autumn the beds get a cover of leaves or a sown crop of rye that holds the soil through the rain. None of this is fast, and none of it is hard. It is a habit more than a method, and the habit is the whole trick. Over a few years the difference shows in the colour of the soil, in how the spade goes in, and in how little the plants sulk in a dry week. That is the reason to keep at it, and the reason this post is long enough to count as the whole article rather than a teaser for one.
